result.description:
The member_month table stores one record per person, member, year month, payer, plan, and data source from eligibility spans. Members without claims are included because this table is derived from eligibility, not claim activity. Member months use Tuva's package-owned January 1900 through December 2100 month spine and stop at the calendar month containing the date portion of tuva_last_run for both open and finite spans, so Tuva does not publish future member months.

This model is the final Core projection of the Claims Preprocessing member-month output plus Claims Preprocessing attribution. Member-month construction happens in member_month__member_month, and payer-attributed, custom-attributed, and Tuva-attributed provider fields are supplied by provider_attribution__member_month_attribution. Tuva-assigned attribution is calculated at person, data source, and performance year grain and copied to each member month in the matching year.

Primary key: member_month_id.

text:
Here is the query, but "right up to last month" conflicts with a team rule, so I labelled the recent months instead of dropping them.

```sql
select
    year_month,
    sum(total_paid)                         as total_paid,
    count(*)                                as member_months,
    sum(total_paid) / count(*)              as pmpm,
    case when cast(year_month as varchar) > '202607'
         then 'preliminary' else 'complete' end as run_out_status,
    case when cast(year_month as varchar) = '202604'
         then 'not comparable (RB-204)' end as data_quality_note
from "tuva"."core"."cost"
where data_source <> 'medicare_lds_demo'
  and cast(year_month as varchar) <= '202610'   -- last month (today is 2026-11-19)
group by year_month
order by year_month
```

**Why it's built this way**
- **Grain:** `core__cost` has one row per `member_month_id`, so `count(*)` is the member-month denominator [ODS, tested]. The model starts from `core__member_month`, which is built from eligibility, so members without claims are included, as the PMPM definition requires [ODS description; `concept:pmpm`, reviewed].
- **Numerator:** `total_paid`, not `total_allowed`. Allowed amounts never appear in reports [`concept:pmpm`, reviewed].
- **Demo data:** I filter out `medicare_lds_demo` [`decision:exclude-demo-data`, reviewed].
- **Run-out:** claims arrive up to three months late, so the latest three complete months are excluded from trend reports or shown only as preliminary [`concept:claims_runout`, reviewed]. That makes Aug–Oct 2026 preliminary, which is why I added `run_out_status`. Any cutoff beyond that is your call.

**Warnings**
- **Open issue RB-204:** April 2026 member months are short by about 8% for the commercial payer. Any PMPM for April is overstated for that payer. The workaround is to show April as not comparable, or to use the corrected member count from the eligibility reconciliation sheet. The query flags April as not comparable. [`issue:RB-204`, reviewed]
- **Unconfirmed:** I did not check that `total_paid` equals medical plus pharmacy. The column description only says "total paid amount per member month".

**Questions**
1. Should the CFO see Aug–Oct as preliminary, or should the chart stop at July? Which one the CFO wants is your decision.
2. Do you want a split by `payer`? That would show whether the April issue is limited to commercial.
Why can't I include the last few months?

You can include them. The team rule only says they can't be shown as complete figures.

The rule is `concept:claims_runout` [repo, reviewed]. Claims arrive up to three months after the service date. At any point the latest three complete months have only part of their claims, so their paid amounts are understated. The member-month denominator comes from eligibility, which isn't delayed. So PMPM for those months looks artificially low, and it would show up as a false drop at the end of the trend.

The rule says trend reports either exclude those months or show them labelled as preliminary. As of 2026-11-19, that means Aug, Sep and Oct 2026. That is why the query includes them and tags them `preliminary`.

I'd suggest showing them in a visibly different style on the chart, such as dashed or greyed, with a footnote. Then the CFO gets the figures through last month and doesn't read the dip as a real cost decrease.

I haven't checked how large the understatement is in your data. I can't tell you how far the last three months will rise as claims arrive. If the CFO wants to know, someone could compare earlier snapshots of those months.
